title: A learned model, its compounding error, and CEM model-predictive control
brief: Fit a linear dynamics model to CartPole, measure how its error grows over an open-loop rollout, then plan through it with the cross-entropy method and balance the pole.
hints: Each row of X is [state, action, 1], so W = solve(X.T @ X + ridge * I, X.T @ next_states). The bias is the last row of W.
rollout must feed step_fn its own previous output. Start a list with s0, append step_fn(list[-1], actions[:, t]) for each t, and stack along axis 1.
k_step_errors is np.linalg.norm(imagined[:, 1:] - real[:, 1:], axis=-1).mean(axis=0), where both come from rollout with the same s0 and actions.
cem_update keeps samples[np.argsort(-scores)[:n_elite]], because higher scores are better, and returns their mean and std along axis 0.
In mpc_action, turn each plan u of shape (H,) into actions (u > 0) of shape (H, 1), start every rollout from the real state, and score the states after the start.
